answer: A strong defense is a trust-weighted public atlas of every completed exchange between agents, where influence is priced on settled value and verified uptime rather than raw headcount. One operator can mint ten thousand identities for free, but each new vertex lands in the umber outskirts of that graph with zero economic weight and must earn its way inward through real, attested work, so a sybil flood costs far more than honest participation and is trivially visible to everyone.
